claims.text: Someone shaping a roundtable in London asked whether the human in the loop is a safety net or a bottleneck.
claims.quote: is the human in the loop a safety net or a bottleneck?

claims.text: A person checking every output is a bottleneck: if every piece of the agent's work waits for a person, the agent runs at the speed of the person.
claims.quote: if every piece of that work waits for a person, the agent runs at the speed of the person

claims.text: Anthropic, writing about its coding agent in March 2026, opened with the number: Claude Code users approve 93% of permission prompts.
claims.quote: Claude Code users approve 93% of permission prompts

claims.text: In October 2025 Anthropic named approval fatigue and reported that sandboxing safely reduces permission prompts by 84%.
claims.quote: safely reduces permission prompts by 84%

value.unit: percent reduction in permission prompts from sandboxing

claims.text: The fix the vendor reached for was fewer prompts, not more attentive people, and the owner thinks that is right.
claims.quote: The fix the vendor reached for was fewer prompts, not more attentive people, and I think that is right.

claims.text: Below a certain level on the agency scale the person is not a safety net; they are where the liability lands for a decision the system made.
claims.quote: They are where the liability lands for a decision the system made

claims.text: Checking every output gives you the cost of a bottleneck and the protection of a rubber stamp.
claims.quote: checking every output gives you the cost of a bottleneck and the protection of a rubber stamp

claims.text: Two questions place every output: can it be undone, and how much would it cost if it were wrong; the person goes where the answers are no and a lot.
claims.quote: can it be undone, and how much would it cost if it were wrong?

claims.text: In the owner's setup the person is at sending: the agents write drafts, and he reads, changes and presses send, because an email in his name cannot be recalled.
claims.quote: the agents write drafts, and I read, change and press send

claims.text: An article can be undone, so nobody approves it before it goes live; validators fail the build on a broken link, a quote not word for word, a banned word or a missing figure.
claims.quote: a validator that fails the build on a broken link, a quote that is not word for word in its source, a banned word or a missing figure

claims.text: The owner reads every article after it is live, and what he finds becomes a new version and, if it is about wording, a rule.
claims.quote: I read every article, but I read it after it is live

claims.text: After two emails went out that should not have, every draft now passes a second reader, a separate model call that sees only the rules, the sources and the draft.
claims.quote: every draft passes a separate model call that sees only the rules, the sources and the draft, and anything but an explicit pass stops it

claims.text: Redesigning one customer service agent three times cut the share of its policy kept only by the model's good behaviour from 97% to 23%, and its reach from 38,000 records to one.
claims.quote: fell from 97% to 23%, and the reach of one run fell from 38,000 customer records to one customer

value.unit: percent of policy rows kept by hope, after against before

claims.text: At the higher levels of the scale a review stops being a sign-off and becomes a quality step: each draft is a chance to fix the rule, the prompt or the data rather than the draft.
claims.quote: each draft is a chance to fix whatever produced it, the rule, the prompt, the data, rather than the draft itself

claims.text: A human in the loop who fixes the source makes the loop need them less every week; one who approves outputs makes it need them exactly as much forever.
claims.quote: A human in the loop who fixes the source makes the loop need them less every week.

claims.text: Trust in the owner's email agents is a record of drafts he did not have to change, the draft's hash beside the email that went out, read whenever he wants.
claims.quote: Trust in my email agents is not a feeling; it is a record of drafts I did not have to change

claims.text: The agent team has one exception written into its policy: a security agent may send one email, to one address, to put the team on hold.
claims.quote: a security agent may send one email, to one address, to put the team on hold

claims.text: Reading the footprint afterwards against the mandate finds the near misses no approval prompt would have shown.
claims.quote: Reading the footprint afterwards against the mandate finds the near misses

claims.text: On 13 October 2026 the newsroom shipped fourteen releases, v0.12.5 to v0.12.18, every commit made by an agent session, none approved by a person before going live.
claims.quote: the newsroom shipped fourteen releases, v0.12.5 to v0.12.18

claims.text: Five articles were written and published in the repository that day, four by this session, each researched, checked, built, validated, tested and leak-scanned by an agent.
claims.quote: Five articles were written and published in this repository.

claims.text: The twelve agents that run the owner's correspondence draft every email and send none, the one exception being the security agent's hold email.
claims.quote: the twelve agents that run my correspondence

claims.text: Shipping on its own and drafting without sending is not a contradiction but the same rule applied to two blast radii: an article can be corrected tomorrow, an email cannot.
claims.quote: An article can be corrected tomorrow. An email cannot.

claims.text: For the roundtable: which of your agent's outputs can be undone, and which cannot, and is the person only on the second kind?
claims.quote: Which of your agent's outputs can be undone, and which cannot?

claims.text: What share of your approvals are yes, and if it is above ninety per cent, what is the check for?
claims.quote: What share of your approvals are yes? If it is above ninety per cent, what is the check for?

claims.text: What record would let you remove a human check next quarter, and who decides?
claims.quote: What record would let you remove a human check next quarter, and who decides?

claims.text: The 93% is one vendor's figure for one product, about permission prompts in a coding agent; other approval flows may differ.
claims.quote: The 93% is one vendor's figure for one product.

claims.text: The owner's production is small: one person, one newsroom, one agent team; the pattern is what he would defend, not the scale.
claims.quote: One person, one newsroom, one agent team.

claims.text: Some outputs need a person by law or by their nature; medicine, law and money moved on someone else's behalf have rules of their own.
claims.quote: Some outputs need a person by law or by their nature.

claims.text: Nobody approving each release is not nobody being responsible: the owner owns what the agents publish, and the controls are his.
claims.quote: I own what the agents publish, and the controls are mine; I chose where to put myself.

claims.text: The roundtable question is paraphrased; it came in a private message and its author is not named.
claims.quote: The roundtable question is paraphrased.

claims.text: There was no voice memo; the article was assembled by the site's agent from the owner's published positions, and the production counts are from the git log for 13 October 2026.
claims.quote: There was no voice memo: this article was assembled by this site's agent from my published positions
